title: Quantile-driven prefill tiering with kernel-demotion and attention-hint routing
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: we observe recurring 95th/99th latency spikes for mixed workloads where long-sequence prefill requests crowd short conversational decodes. Current phase-splitting heuristics use static size thresholds and do not consider attention sparsity or kernel congestion signals, which leads to inefficient kernel choices (full-precision kernels used for thin sequences) and unfair tenant slowdowns.

Goal: implement a quantile-driven prefill tiering policy that: (1) uses per-model sequence-length histograms to pick dynamic split quantiles, (2) probes attention sparsity at prefill to tag requests with attention-hint flags, and (3) emits kernel-demotion signals (soft-demotion to lower-cost kernels or quantized variants) when backpressure/kernels are overloaded. The scheduler should balance latency SLOs (P95 target) against throughput/cost objectives and maintain tenant fairness via soft-credit decay.

Scope: scheduling policy + runtime hooks. No model architecture changes. Changes touch: arbitration layer, prefill probe phase, kernel selector, and the metrics/tuning dashboard.

Out-of-scope: changes to model weights or persistent quantization. Dedicated capacity autoscaler changes will be handled separately if needed.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler can compute split quantile per model from rolling 24h sequence histogram
Requests are annotated with attention-hint flags from a <5ms probe during prefill
Kernel selector accepts soft-demote flags and prefers quantized-compatible kernels when signaled
P95 latency for short decodes improves by >=15% for mixed workloads in internal perf suite
Overall cost per token for mixed workload decreases by >=5% without increasing error rate beyond baseline eval thresholds
Dashboard shows per-model quantile, attention-sparsity distribution, kernel-demotion rate, and tenant fairness score
